title: Which file gets loaded?
description:
Simulate the standard DLL search order for a request by name. Write

```cpp
struct Machine
{
    std::string appDir;                          // e.g. "C:\\Games\\Xenon"
    std::string currentDir;
    std::vector<std::string> pathDirs;           // PATH, in order
    std::set<std::string> files;                 // every file that exists, as full paths
    std::set<std::string> knownDlls;             // names of known DLLs
    std::set<std::string> alreadyLoaded;         // full paths of modules already in the process
};

std::string findDll(const Machine& m, const std::string& name);
```

Return the full path that would be loaded, or an empty string if none is found. Folders are joined to the name with one backslash: `appDir + "\\" + name`.

The order:

1. **Already loaded**: if any full path in `alreadyLoaded` ends with `"\\" + name`, return that path.
2. **Known DLLs**: if `name` is in `knownDlls`, return `"C:\\Windows\\System32\\" + name` (whether or not it is in `files`).
3. Then the first folder, in this order, where the file exists: `appDir`, `C:\Windows\System32`, `C:\Windows\System`, `C:\Windows`, `currentDir`, then each folder of `pathDirs`.

Upper and lower case **do** matter in this simulation: compare names exactly.
hints: For "already loaded", compare the end of each loaded path with `"\\" + name`, including the backslash, so `notStoneMath.dll` does not match `StoneMath.dll`.
